mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC mobility has shown a slight recovery from its recent low at t-2w. This indicates a slow but steady return of consumer activity, which will continue to drive RETAIL_REC upwards over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the last 28 days, or shows no significant improvement from the t-0w level.

mechanism_narrative: The significant rebound in PARKS mobility at t-0w suggests an increased willingness among residents to leave their homes for leisure. This increased comfort with public spaces will translate into higher RETAIL_REC within the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 percentage points week-on-week.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility increases by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC does not show an increase over the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent upward trend in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility signals a return to office-based work and associated commuting patterns. This will directly increase weekday foot traffic in retail areas, boosting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show week-on-week increases.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC remains stagnant or declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The slight decrease in RESIDENTIAL mobility at t-0w, following a period of increase, indicates a shift towards spending less time at home. This behavioral change, in a reopening context, will free up time for out-of-home activities, including retail and recreation, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Despite minor recent upticks, all mobility indices remain significantly below baseline, indicating a persistent underlying reluctance for non-essential activities. This sustained low level of overall activity will continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a sustained increase over the next four weeks, exceeding -55% from baseline.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in essential GROCERY_PHARM visits signals a rising baseline comfort level with public spaces. If this comfort continues to grow, it will spill over into non-essential RETAIL_REC, leading to an increase over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM increases week-on-week for two consecutive weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM increases for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC remains flat or declines in the subsequent two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility increases and RESIDENTIAL mobility decreases, it signifies a clear shift in daily routines away from home and towards work. This shift creates more opportunities for incidental retail and recreation stops, positively impacting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES increases while RESIDENTIAL decreases week-on-week.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES increases and RESIDENTIAL decreases for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC does not improve over the subsequent four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The strong rebound in PARKS mobility at t-0w, likely influenced by improving weather conditions, indicates a broader increase in outdoor activity and willingness to leave home. This seasonal shift will immediately and positively impact RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS mobility is above -40% from baseline.
failure_condition: PARKS mobility remains above -40% from baseline, but RETAIL_REC declines in the immediate next week.
